subject: Audit log export & immutability — acceptance criteria and next steps
content:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Subject: Audit log export & immutability — acceptance criteria and next steps

Hi Lydia / Chris —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our security/discovery call and a proposed acceptance-criteria checklist so your InfoSec team can validate the audit/logging capabilities against MediProspect requirements. I pulled the items we discussed into a short list and attached a draft spec and a sample CSV for your review.

Call recap (high-level)
- Redwood provides admin activity logs + API request logs; logs include actor, timestamp (UTC), request path, resource id, response code, and a KV diff where applicable.
- Export options: on-demand CSV/NDJSON + scheduled delivery to customer S3 bucket; optional signed manifests for immutability.
- Retention & immutability: configurable retention policies per-account; we support write-once manifests and signed checksums to help meet audit requirements.

Proposed acceptance criteria (please mark ok / need more detail):
1) Export format: NDJSON or CSV with header row and RFC3339 timestamps — sample attached.
2) Export delivery: push to customer S3 (pre-signed, cross-account role) OR temporary secure download link (signed URL).
3) Immutability proof: SHA256 checksums plus a signed manifest; optional GPG-signed archive for long-term storage.
4) Retention controls: ability to set min-retention window (e.g., 90/365 days) and retention-lock for regulatory holds.
5) Access logs: we provide separate audit of export activity (who exported, when, destination).
6) Forensic needs: ability to export full KV cache snapshots on request for incident investigations (48–72 hour SLA for first export with Dedicated customers).

Next steps I propose:
- Lydia: confirm any items above that are mandatory vs. advisory for MediProspect (we highlighted the ones we think are must-haves in the attachment).
- Redwood (Ben): provide a short technical appendix on export signing/manifest workflow and a sample API call (Ben included below / attachment).
- Schedule a 30-min evidence review with your InfoSec to walk through the sample export and manifest. Suggested times below.

Attachments: redwood-audit-export-spec-v1.pdf (draft spec), sample-admin-activity-log.csv (sample data)

Suggested meeting slots (PST): Wed 5/5 10:00–10:30, Thu 5/6 14:00–14:30 — let me know what works and I will send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Ava Chen

Thanks Ava — useful summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we loop in the rest of InfoSec: 

1) When you say "signed manifests", can you confirm whether the manifest is generated and signed by Redwood and if the signature is verifiable by an external key (i.e., we can store the public key in our KMS for later verification)?
2) For the S3 push option: do you support cross-account role assumptions (we prefer an AWS PutObject to a bucket in our account using a short-lived role), or do you only use pre-signed URLs?
3) Retention-lock: can you provide the exact behavior? If we request a regulatory hold, does Redwood prevent deletes for the hold window regardless of retention policy changes?
4) Sample export frequency: can we get a continuous export (near-real-time streaming to S3) or is it batched (hourly/daily)?

Also, for compliance we need a statement on whether audit logs contain PII fields — if any PII appears in KV diffs is it redacted by default or configurable?

If you can answer the above in writing, we can confirm the required items and I will circulate to our legal & InfoSec.

Regards,
Lydia Park
InfoSec Manager | MediProspect
lydia.park@mediprospect.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Audit log export & immutability — acceptance criteria and next steps

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline below and a technical appendix attached.

1) Signed manifests
- Manifest generation: Redwood generates the manifest at export time. The manifest contains file names, SHA256 checksums, file sizes, and a UTC timestamp.
- Signature model: we sign the manifest using a Redwood signing key (RSA-2048) and also provide the raw manifest + signature so you can verify using our public key. We can rotate keys and publish the public key to a customer-facing endpoint. If you need to store the public key in your KMS for future verification that works fine.

2) S3 delivery options
- Supported: cross-account PutObject using a short-lived role assumption (recommended), pre-signed URLs (we support both), and direct push to partner-managed buckets. We recommend cross-account role for largest customers.

3) Retention-lock / holds
- Behavior: when a regulatory hold is applied at the account level, Redwood will not delete or mutate any objects covered by the hold. Holds are enforced in the control plane and audited. The hold can only be released by a designated set of users (configurable via roles). We will provide an API and UI controls for applying/releasing holds.

4) Export frequency
- Options: near-real-time streaming (Kafka/Firehose to S3 with per-minute batched files) for Dedicated customers, or batched exports (hourly/daily) for hosted customers.

PII in logs
- Default behavior: PII is not included in structured actor fields (actor id is an internal id). KV diffs can contain user-provided content depending on how your product uses the API. By default we redact common PII fields (email, SSN, phone) in the KV diff for hosted customers. For Dedicated / Private deployments you can choose redaction config to match your policy.

Attached: redwood-audit-export-spec-v1.pdf (technical appendix), sample-admin-activity-log.csv, and a short checklist snippet. Also pasted below is an example API call for an on-demand export:

POST /v1/admin/logs/export
Request body: { "format": "ndjson", "from": "2027-05-01T00:00:00Z", "to": "2027-05-03T23:59:59Z", "delivery": { "type": "s3", "role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodExportWriter", "bucket": "mp-audit-exports" } }

Response: 202 Accepted + manifest URL (signed)

Let me know if you want a concrete sample manifest — I included one in the PDF.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
